definition: Mathematical linguistics is the application of mathematics to model phenomena and solve problems in general linguistics and theoretical linguistics.
details: Mathematical linguistics has a significant amount of overlap with computational linguistics.

explainer.lead: Mathematical linguistics uses mathematics to model linguistic phenomena and solve problems in general and theoretical linguistics. It overlaps heavily with computational linguistics, so the two are often confused.

tiers.eli5: It is using maths — sets, rules, statistics — to describe how language works, rather than just learning languages.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers borrow formalisms such as formal grammars and statistical models when building language systems. The pitfall is assuming a mathematical model of language is automatically a working computational system.
tiers.paperLevel: Formal and mathematical methods applied to general and theoretical linguistics; substantial overlap with computational linguistics.

explainer.example: A researcher writes a formal grammar for a fragment of English and proves properties about which strings it generates.
